title: Big Data Methods for Statistics
curriculum_locator: Stat H-308 Big Data Methods for Statistics; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: The Statistical Geometry of High Dimensions
scope: The curse of dimensionality in statistical learning: exponential volume scaling and data sparsity in high-dimensional Euclidean space R^p
Volume of high-dimensional unit hyperspheres and hypercubes: derivation of V_p(R) via Gamma function and asymptotic collapse to zero
Concentration of measure phenomenon: Gaussian isoperimetric inequality and concentration around thin spherical shells
Distance concentration: asymptotic behavior of pairwise Euclidean distances lim_(p->infinity) (D_max - D_min)/D_min = 0
Near-orthogonality of random vectors in high dimensions: inner product concentration and angle distribution
The empty space phenomenon and its profound implications for non-parametric density estimation and kernel smoothing

units.title: Large-Scale Dimension Reduction: Spectral & Manifold Learning
scope: High-dimensional Principal Component Analysis (PCA) when p >> n: breakdown of empirical covariance matrix consistency
Random matrix theory: the Marchenko-Pastur distribution for sample eigenvalues under null noise
Spiked covariance models, BBP phase transition (Baik-Ben Arous-Péché), and spectral thresholding
Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) at massive scale: economy-size SVD and power iteration
Randomized SVD (Halko-Martinsson-Tropp framework): random Gaussian test matrices and error bounds

Non-linear manifold learning: Multidimensional Scaling (MDS), t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) with Kullback-Leibler divergence, and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)

units.title: Sparse Statistical Learning & Regularization (Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net)
scope: Linear regression in the high-dimensional regime (p >> n): singularity of X^T X and ill-posed ordinary least squares
Ridge regression (L2 regularization): penalization objective, analytical solution beta_hat_ridge = (X^T X + lambda I)^(-1) X^T y, and singular value shrinkage
The Lasso (L1 regularization, Tibshirani 1996): geometry of the L1 diamond constraint, exact sparsity, and variable selection
Subgradient calculus and coordinate descent algorithm for Lasso: soft-thresholding operator S(z, lambda) = sign(z) max(0, |z| - lambda)
The Elastic Net (Zou & Hastie): combining L1 and L2 penalties to address grouped variable selection and collinearity
Asymptotic oracle properties: Fan and Li criteria, Adaptive Lasso, and non-convex penalties (SCAD and MCP)

units.title: Distributed Computing Foundations: MapReduce, Hadoop & Spark for Statisticians
scope: Architectures for massive datasets: shared-memory multiprocessing vs distributed-memory shared-nothing clusters
The MapReduce computing paradigm: key-value pairs, map functions, shuffle-and-sort phase, and reduce aggregation
Computing sufficient statistics in parallel: embarrassingly parallel computations, sample moments, contingency tables, and gradient accumulation
Apache Spark architecture: Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs), lineage graphs, transformations vs actions, and in-memory caching
Spark DataFrames and distributed MLlib: parallel matrix computations and distributed regression models
Communication complexity vs computational complexity in distributed statistical estimation

units.title: First-Order Stochastic Optimization for Massive Data
scope: Convex optimization foundations in statistical machine learning: Lipschitz continuous gradients and strong convexity
Batch Gradient Descent (GD) and its computational intractability on massive sample sizes (O(n) per update)
Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD, Robbins-Monro): unbiased gradient estimation via random single-sample draws, update rule, and O(1) per-step complexity
Convergence rates of SGD for convex and strongly convex loss functions: sublinear O(1/sqrt(k)) and O(1/k) bounds
Mini-batch SGD: balancing variance reduction with vectorization hardware efficiency
Accelerated and adaptive stochastic optimizers: Polyak momentum, Nesterov accelerated gradient, AdaGrad, RMSprop, and the Adam optimizer
Asynchronous distributed SGD (Hogwild! framework) and communication-efficient parallel optimization

units.title: Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra (RandNLA)
scope: The RandNLA paradigm: using deliberate algorithmic randomness to accelerate matrix computations on massive datasets
Matrix sketching and dimension reduction: embedding high-dimensional matrices into lower-dimensional sketch spaces
The Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma: metric-preserving random projections, epsilon-isometries, and minimum projection dimension k >= O(epsilon^(-2) ln n)
Random projection matrices: Gaussian random matrices, Rademacher matrices, and the Subsampled Randomized Hadamard Transform (SRHT)
Randomized approximate matrix multiplication: probability proportional to Euclidean norm squared
Leverage score sampling: statistical leverage scores h_ii = x_i^T (X^T X)^(-1) x_i, CUR matrix decompositions, and subspace embeddings

units.title: Streaming Data, Online Learning & One-Pass Sketching Algorithms
scope: The data stream model: continuous, unbounded, high-velocity data flows where storage and multiple passes are impossible
One-pass streaming estimation of summary statistics: Welford's streaming algorithm for mean and variance
Reservoir Sampling: Algorithm R (Vitter) for generating a uniform random sample of size k from an unknown stream length N
The Count-Min Sketch (Cormode & Muthukrishnan): hashing data items into 2D count arrays, point query estimation, and heavy hitter detection
The HyperLogLog algorithm (Flajolet et al.): estimating distinct cardinality using leading-zero bit patterns and harmonic mean aggregation
Online learning and concept drift: adaptive windowing (ADWIN) and streaming regression models with fading memory weights

units.title: High-Dimensional Multiple Testing & False Discovery Rate (FDR)
scope: The multiple testing crisis in high-dimensional science (genomics, proteomics, digital A/B testing): simultaneous evaluation of m >> 10^4 hypotheses
Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER): definition P(V >= 1), union bound, Bonferroni correction alpha/m, and Sidak correction
Sequential rejection procedures: Holm-Bonferroni step-down test and Hochberg step-up test
The False Discovery Rate (FDR, Benjamini & Hochberg 1995): definition FDR = E[V / max(R, 1)]
The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) step-up procedure: ranking p-values p_(1) <= p_(2) <= ... <= p_(m) and critical threshold lines
Proof of FDR control under independence and positive regression dependency (PRDS)
Storey's positive FDR (pFDR) and q-value methodology: estimating the proportion of true null hypotheses pi_0
Empirical Bayes multiple testing: Bradley Efron's Local False Discovery Rate (lfdr) and two-groups mixture model f(z) = pi_0 f_0(z) + (1 - pi_0) f_1(z)
